claude.rationale: This was an internal reorganization merging an intermediate holding-company tier (Accenture Holdings plc) into its top-level public parent (Accenture plc), which already controlled and consolidated it; the deal was described as "internal and administrative in nature" with "no effect on ... how Accenture goes to market, how it manages its business or how it serves its clients." T3 collapses two legal tiers into one (N-1) via merger with only asset/liability transfer, share exchange, and contract substitution; Accenture Holdings is "not presented as an independently run operating business with its own product, process, or personnel functions," so no customer-facing product (T4) or operating process/people (T5/T6) crossed a boundary independently — hence gap_45=0 and gap_56=0, as no product or process moved apart from processes or people already sitting in the unaffected consolidated operating subsidiaries.

grok.rationale: The slice states the merger was 'internal and administrative in nature' with 'no effect on ... how Accenture goes to market, how it manages its business or how it serves its clients,' and that Accenture Holdings 'is not presented as an independently run operating business with its own product, process, or personnel functions apart from Accenture plc's existing consolidated operations.' Accordingly neither a distinct T4 product nor a distinct T5 process crossed the boundary as separable operating layers, so gap_45 = 0; likewise no T5 process transferred apart from T6 organization, so gap_56 = 0. No transitional-services or operating agreement is disclosed because no such substrate gap existed at closing.

openai.rationale: The filing described the merger as internal and administrative, with no effect on how Accenture goes to market, manages its business, or serves clients. Accenture Holdings was not presented as having independent product, process, or personnel functions; therefore, no customer-facing product crossed without its processes, and no processes crossed without the organization that operated them.
